newsitem.title: DUBAI: Thousands of Iranians hold anti-Israel protest.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of Iranians hold anti-Israel protest.

text.p: About 10,000 Iranians chanting "Death to Israel" demonstrated in front of a U.N. office in Tehran on Sunday, protesting against Israel's alleged responsibility for posters depicting Islam's Prophet Mohammad as a pig.
The United Nations main office in Tehran was surrounded by police forces and protected by barriers. Police also blocked the street to traffic.
The crowds, including women in long black chador robes, began the protest at 10 a.m. (0530 GMT), chanting "Death to America" and "Death to Israel", witnesses said.
Demonstrators carried banners and posters condemning "Israel's sacrilege against Islam and the holy Prophet Mohammad" and calling for the destruction of the Jewish state.
The protesters were referring to the pasting of posters in the West Bank town of Hebron depicting Prophet Mohammad as a pig stamping on the Koran with one hoof and writing in it with another.
Israeli leaders have condemned the anti-Moslem posters and a 26-year-old Jewish woman has been charged with illegally posting the signs.

Islam's highest Sunni Moslem religious authority Sheikh Mohammad Sayyed Tantawi, Grand Mufti of the prestigious al-Azhar mosque in Cairo, and some Iranian Shi'ite clerics have said the person who pasted the posters must be killed for desecration.
Members of the military police attending the Tehran rally wore gold-coloured bands across their chests with the words "Death to Israel" printed on them in red letters.
Some protesters erected large posters of the late Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini and Iran's spiritual leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei opposite the U.N. premises.
A member of the militant Ansar-e Hizbollah (Supporters of the Party of God), led the chorus of chants, calling to demonstrators from the top of a delapidated pick-up truck.
The rally concluded after two-and-a-half hours with demonstrators reading out a resolution condemning Israel, supported by chants of "God is Greatest" from the crowds.
The head of Iran's judiciary, Ayatollah Mohammad Yazdi, said at a mass prayer gathering on Friday Israel deserved to be destroyed because of the posters.
"Israel should be razed to the ground because it has moved against Islam and Islam's prophet," the senior cleric said.
